title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The programme in Niger helps to improve access to basic needs and the rights to life, access to food, water, shelter and medical assistance for vulnerable people affected by humanitarian crises in 35 communities in Ouallam, Mirriah and Gouré in Niger. In 2024, GOAL directly reached 40,052 people in various sectors. Thanks to this programme, women's empowerment and decision-making are improved within communities through income-generating activities (VSLA). Access to basic healthcare is improved for people, particularly women and children, in areas where access to sanitation facilities is difficult. The programme supports vulnerable households and people with disabilities affected by multiple shocks. In addition, the programme provides access to smart farming techniques adapted to climate change in rural communities to improve diversification and consumption of a variety of micronutrient-rich foods.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 2: People Have Resilient Health. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Social Behaviour Change (SBC) approaches are used to build community and household capacity to care for their own health – including Care Groups, Men’s Health Groups, and community based reproductive health volunteers who work to increase the demand for health services. Social and gender norms are being addressed through Community Conversations on women’s empowerment, reproductive health and family planning to support the uptake of RMNCHN services.
